paragraphs.title: Opening the Vision and Seeking the Meaning of Jeremiah’s Prophecy

answers: Cyrus
Darius the son of Ahasuerus
Nebuchadnezzar
easy.explanation: Daniel 9:1 identifies the time as the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus.
easy.q: Who was king in the year described at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: Books
The king’s letters
Military records
easy.explanation: Daniel says, “I Daniel understood by books.”
easy.q: What did Daniel understand by studying?

answers: Seven years
Seven hundred years
Seventy years
easy.explanation: The prophecy concerned seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years were mentioned in Jeremiah’s prophecy?

answers: The number of Babylonian kings
The seventy years of Jerusalem’s desolation
The time of the Exodus
medium.explanation: Daniel studied the books to understand the seventy years appointed for Jerusalem’s desolation.
medium.q: What was Daniel seeking to understand?

answers: He believed Babylon’s fall had solved every problem
He did not know that Babylon had fallen
He understood that Babylon’s fall had not yet brought redemption
medium.explanation: The passage presents Daniel as seeking to understand why Jerusalem’s restoration had not yet fully come.
medium.q: Why was Daniel still seeking meaning after Babylon’s fall?

answers: Ruins and devastated places
Celebrations
Treasures
medium.explanation: “Desolations” refers to places that have been ruined, laid waste, or left empty.
medium.q: What does “desolations” mean in the phrase “the desolations of Jerusalem”?

answers: He was seeking to understand the meaning of the prophecy
He rejected the words of the prophets
He was concerned only with describing the king
challenge.explanation: Daniel’s study of the books shows that he was seeking understanding concerning Jeremiah’s prophecy.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Daniel’s study of the prophetic writings?

answers: It identifies the time when Daniel studied the prophecy
It identifies the year Jeremiah was born
It identifies the end of all seventy years
challenge.explanation: The verse places Daniel’s study in a specific historical setting: the first year of Darius’s reign.
challenge.q: Why is the first year of Darius important at the opening of the passage?

answers: The tension between reading books and forgetting them
The tension between expecting restoration and seeing Jerusalem still desolate
The tension between Darius and the king of Egypt
challenge.explanation: Daniel sees a difference between Babylon’s fall and the complete restoration of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What tension appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Fasting, Confession, and Recognition of Sin

answers: With prayer, fasting, sackcloth, and ashes
With singing and dancing
With war and judgment
easy.explanation: Daniel set his face to the Lord with prayer and supplications, fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
easy.q: How did Daniel seek the Lord?

answers: The king alone
The whole people
Jeremiah the prophet
easy.explanation: Daniel’s confession includes the people, their rulers, and their fathers, not merely himself.
easy.q: On whose behalf did Daniel confess?

answers: They had failed to hear the prophets and had departed from God’s law
They had failed to build a palace
They had failed to study the royal records
easy.explanation: Daniel says they had not hearkened to the prophets and had departed from God’s precepts and judgments.
easy.q: What had the people done according to the confession?

answers: Disobedience was connected with the curse and the great evil that came upon them
Disobedience removed the curse
The passage makes no connection between them
medium.explanation: Daniel explains that because the people sinned and did not obey, the foretold curse and evil came upon them.
medium.q: What connection does Daniel make between disobedience and the troubles that came upon the people?

answers: Only the common people
Only the kings
The people, kings, princes, and fathers
medium.explanation: Daniel speaks of the whole people and their leaders and ancestors as having sinned.
medium.q: Who is included in responsibility for the sin?

answers: We have resisted God and refused to obey Him
We have praised God
We have asked God a question
medium.explanation: To rebel is to resist authority and refuse obedience.
medium.q: What does “we have rebelled” mean in this confession?

answers: It expresses shared responsibility for the people’s sin
It describes only Daniel’s personal sin
It places the blame on the prophets alone
challenge.explanation: Daniel confesses in solidarity with the people and therefore uses inclusive language such as “we.”
challenge.q: Why does the confession repeatedly use the word “we”?

answers: It shows that the people sinned against instruction already given
It proves that no warnings had been given
It presents the law as merely a historical book
challenge.explanation: The law and the prophets had already instructed and warned the people, making their disobedience deliberate.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of mentioning the law and the prophets?

answers: The people believe the judgment is unfair
The people acknowledge God’s justice and their own responsibility
The Lord has no connection with human actions
challenge.explanation: Daniel declares God righteous while acknowledging that the people had not obeyed His voice.
challenge.q: What does Daniel’s statement that righteousness belongs to the Lord imply when trouble has come?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Mercy for Jerusalem and God’s Name

answers: The Exodus from Egypt
The building of the temple
A war fought by Darius
easy.explanation: Daniel recalls that the Lord brought His people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand.
easy.q: What past event does Daniel recall?

answers: Honor
The Lord’s anger and fury
Peace
easy.explanation: Daniel asks that the Lord’s anger and fury be turned away from Jerusalem.
easy.q: What does Daniel ask to be turned away from Jerusalem?

answers: The Lord’s mercies
The Lord’s name
The people’s righteousnesses
easy.explanation: Daniel says, “we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies.”
easy.q: What does Daniel specifically say he is not relying on?

answers: For His own sake and name
For the king’s wealth
For the success of a foreign army
medium.explanation: Daniel asks the Lord to act for His own sake because Jerusalem and the people are called by His name.
medium.q: For whose sake does Daniel ask the Lord to hear and act?

answers: That it remain desolate
That the Lord’s face shine upon the desolate sanctuary
That it be moved to another city
medium.explanation: Daniel asks God to cause His face to shine upon His sanctuary that is desolate.
medium.q: What does Daniel request concerning the sanctuary?

answers: Humble requests for mercy and help
Commands for battle
Songs of victory
medium.explanation: Supplications are earnest and humble requests made for mercy or assistance.
medium.q: What does “supplications” mean in this prayer?

answers: Relying on human merit versus relying on God’s mercy
Jerusalem versus Egypt alone
Fasting versus feasting
challenge.explanation: Daniel does not appeal to the people’s righteousness but to God’s great mercies.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Daniel’s request?

answers: The city is called by God’s name, so its condition concerns His honor
The city has no connection with God’s name
Jerusalem is presented as unrelated to God’s people
challenge.explanation: Daniel repeatedly notes that Jerusalem and the people are called by God’s name.
challenge.q: How are Jerusalem and God’s name connected in the prayer?

answers: The urgency and intensity of Daniel’s supplication
The cancellation of Daniel’s confession
That Daniel is asking for nothing
challenge.explanation: The repeated appeals emphasize Daniel’s urgent plea for God to listen, forgive, and act.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated requests “hear,” “forgive,” and “hearken”?

answers: Jeremiah
Gabriel
Darius
easy.explanation: The passage says that the man Gabriel came to Daniel.
easy.q: Who came to Daniel while he was praying?

answers: About the time of the evening oblation
At midnight
At the beginning of the year
easy.explanation: Gabriel came swiftly about the time of the evening offering.

answers: Victory in battle
Skill and understanding
A letter to the king
easy.explanation: Gabriel says he came to give Daniel skill and understanding.
easy.q: What did Gabriel come to give Daniel?

answers: Only after Daniel finished praying
At the beginning of Daniel’s supplications
It never went forth
medium.explanation: Gabriel says, “At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth.”
medium.q: When did the commandment concerning Daniel’s answer go forth?

answers: Gabriel comes while Daniel is praying and brings an answer
Gabriel comes before Daniel begins praying
Gabriel prevents Daniel from praying
medium.explanation: Gabriel arrives while Daniel is speaking, praying, and confessing.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Daniel’s prayer and Gabriel’s appearance?

answers: Gabriel arrived very quickly
Gabriel stood without moving
Gabriel slowly disappeared
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the speed of Gabriel’s arrival.
medium.q: What does “caused to fly swiftly” communicate?

answers: Daniel is presented as highly valued and favored before God
Daniel is presented as an enemy
Daniel is unworthy of receiving an answer
challenge.explanation: The title appears as Gabriel comes to reveal understanding to Daniel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Gabriel calling Daniel “greatly beloved”?

answers: The passage moves from prayer and supplication to revealed explanation
The passage moves from warfare to celebration
The passage moves from kingdoms to the Exodus
challenge.explanation: Daniel’s prayer is followed by Gabriel’s arrival and explanation of the vision.
challenge.q: What transition occurs in this passage?

answers: They prepare Daniel to receive the detailed meaning of the vision
They end the vision without explanation
They send Daniel back only to Jeremiah’s writings
challenge.explanation: Gabriel directs Daniel to think carefully about the revelation he is about to receive.
challenge.q: Why are the commands “understand the matter” and “consider the vision” important?

paragraphs.title: The Seventy Weeks and the Long Path to Restoration

answers: Daniel’s people and the holy city
One king alone
Jeremiah the prophet alone
easy.explanation: Gabriel says that seventy weeks are determined upon Daniel’s people and the holy city.
easy.q: Upon whom were seventy weeks determined?

answers: Bringing in everlasting righteousness
Increasing the king’s army
Building a new city in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The prophecy includes bringing in everlasting righteousness among its purposes.
easy.q: Which purpose is associated with the seventy weeks?

answers: The sacrifice and oblation would cease
Jerusalem would immediately be rebuilt
The seventy weeks would begin
easy.explanation: The prophecy says that in the midst of the week the sacrifice and oblation would cease.
easy.q: What would happen in the midst of the week?

answers: Rebuilding, trouble, the cutting off of Messiah, destruction, and desolation
Celebration, peace, trade, and victory
The Exodus, the giving of the law, and the building of the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The prophecy includes rebuilding Jerusalem, troublous times, Messiah being cut off, destruction, and desolation.
medium.q: What is the central sequence of events described in the vision?

answers: The period aims to finish transgression, make reconciliation, and bring righteousness
The period is intended to extend sin
The vision contains no connection between sin and restoration
medium.explanation: The stated purposes include finishing transgression, making an end of sins, reconciling iniquity, and bringing righteousness.
medium.q: What relationship between sin and restoration appears in the purpose of the seventy weeks?

answers: Laid waste or made empty
Filled with joy
Prepared for a feast
medium.explanation: “Desolate” describes something ruined, devastated, or left empty.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in the final verse?

answers: The vision includes desolation and trouble but also rebuilding, reconciliation, and righteousness
The vision describes only destruction with no purpose of restoration
The vision describes only rebuilding without difficulty
challenge.explanation: Alongside destruction and desolation, the prophecy speaks of rebuilding, reconciliation, righteousness, and holiness.
challenge.q: How do destruction and hope appear together in the vision?

answers: The vision includes a movement from ruin toward restoration
Jerusalem has no connection with the vision
The desolation is presented as the only possible final state
challenge.explanation: The prophecy connects Jerusalem’s restoration and rebuilding with the larger unfolding of the vision.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the command to restore and build Jerusalem?

answers: Seven weeks are mentioned first, followed by threescore and two weeks
One year is mentioned first, followed by one year
Seventy kings are mentioned first, followed by two kings
challenge.explanation: Daniel 9:25 distinguishes seven weeks from the following threescore and two weeks.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between the beginning and the continuation of the period?
